subject: Maths
title: Tree diagrams
subtitle: Probability · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can draw and use tree diagrams to calculate probabilities of combined events.

key_vocab.definition: A tree diagram shows all possible outcomes of two or more events. Each branch represents a probability, and branches from the same point sum to 1.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can draw and use tree diagrams to calculate probabilities of combined events.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Tree diagrams -- A tree diagram shows all possible outcomes of two or more events. Each branch represents a probability, and branches from the same point sum to 1.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Multiply along branches (AND), add between paths (OR). Each set of branches sums to 1.
P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B|A)
Along = multiply, Between = add

Key examples:
  ✓ Multiply along branches for AND  (P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B))
  ✓ Add separate paths for OR  (different routes)
  ✓ All branches from a point sum to 1  (exhaustive)
  ✗ Add along branches for AND  (must multiply)
  ✗ Multiply between paths for OR  (must add)

sections.title: Worked Example
Two-coin problems
sections.content:
Two fair coins are tossed. Find each probability.

(a) P(both tails)
(b) P(one head, one tail)
(c) P(at least one tail)
(d) P(no tails)

sections.title: Die and coin
sections.content:
A coin is tossed and a die is rolled. Find:

(a) P(head and 6)
(b) P(tail and even)
(c) P(head and prime)
(d) P(tail and less than 3)

sections.title: Without replacement
sections.content:
Bag: 4 red, 6 blue. Two drawn without replacement.

(a) P(both red)
(b) P(both blue)
(c) P(one of each colour)
(d) P(at least one red)

sections.title: Real-world tree diagrams
sections.content:
P(bus late) = 0.2, P(train late) = 0.1. Independent.

(a) P(both late)
(b) P(neither late)
(c) P(exactly one late)
(d) P(at least one late)

sections.title: Mixed tree diagram problems
sections.content:
Draw a tree diagram for each and calculate.

(a) 3 coins: P(all heads)
(b) 3 coins: P(exactly 2 heads)
(c) Bag: 5 red, 3 blue. Two picks WITH replacement. P(same colour)
(d) P(win) = 0.6. Two games. P(win both)
(e) P(win) = 0.6. Two games. P(win exactly one)

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Multiply along branches for AND
✗ Add along branches for combined events
✓ Without replacement changes the denominator
✓ P(at least one) = 1 - P(none)
✗ With and without replacement give the same answers
